fatal_errors: The proposed Cr-addition intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of controlled intermediate-temperature aging of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1, which already contains Cr.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as a generic single-phase solid solution rather than the target FCC+B2 eutectic microstructure.
No specific thermal window, exposure duration, or loading regime is defined, so the hypothesis is not operationally testable under the relevant 550–750 °C aging regime.
The proposed mechanism omits L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, and phase-boundary-tip stress concentrations.

The cited evidence does not support prevention of detrimental phase formation by Cr: E1 reports Cr-induced Laves-phase formation, E2 reports B2+BCC decomposition, and E3 reports BCC precipitation after exposure.
The predicted monotonic preservation of toughness misses the observed non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition, including minimum ductility near 600 °C and recovery near 750 °C.
explanation: The response only aligns at the broad level of addressing an HEA subjected to thermal exposure and mechanical testing. It does not reconstruct the alloy, intervention, temperature-dependent transition, structural mediators, or mechanism of the target study. Its baseline comparison with a Cr-free alloy is experimentally possible but irrelevant to an alloy whose target composition already includes Cr. The proposed experiment measures general toughness and phase composition, but its falsification rule merely restates the desired outcome and does not discriminate solid-solution stabilization from ordering- and phase-boundary-controlled embrittlement. A discriminating test would age the same AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy below 550 °C, near 600 °C, near 750 °C, and above 750 °C, then correlate tensile ductility with L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 boundary density, dislocation pile-ups, and crack initiation at boundary tips using TEM or TKD while excluding impurity-segregation-driven intergranular fracture.
